bounded_public_probe_proposal.script:
ExUnit.start(seed: 33011, max_cases: 1)

defmodule GaoxyPublicPreHeadCancelRepeatProbe do
  use ExUnit.Case, async: false
  alias HTTP.{Promise, RequestCompletion}
  @timeout 3_000

  # Exactly32 distinct tests; retain every result and all failures. No retry-to-green.
  for index <- 1..32 do
    @probe_index index
    test "public pre-head cancellation round #{index}" do
      {url, peer} = peer(fn socket, owner ->
        recv_head(socket)
        send(owner, {:request_headers, self()})
        :gen_tcp.recv(socket, 0, @timeout)
      end)
      promise = fetch(url)
      completion = Promise.completion(promise)
      headers = receive do
        {:request_headers, ^peer} -> :received
      after
        @timeout -> :request_headers_timeout
      end
      before_abort = capture(fn -> RequestCompletion.await(completion, 0) end)
      abort = capture(fn -> RequestCompletion.abort_and_await(completion, @timeout) end)
      promise_result = capture(fn -> Promise.await(promise, @timeout) end)

      # Capture both peer result and real owned-peer DOWN even if Promise is unexpected.
      peer_monitor = Process.monitor(peer)
      peer_terminal = receive do
        {:peer_result, ^peer, value} -> value
        {:peer_error, ^peer, error} -> {:peer_error, error}
      after
        @timeout -> :peer_result_timeout
      end
      peer_down = receive do
        {:DOWN, ^peer_monitor, :process, ^peer, reason} -> reason
      after
        @timeout -> :peer_down_timeout
      end
      Process.demonitor(peer_monitor, [:flush])
      repeated = capture(fn -> RequestCompletion.abort_and_await(completion, 0) end)
      row = %{round: @probe_index, request_headers: inspect(headers),
        cleanup_before_abort: inspect(before_abort), abort_and_await: inspect(abort),
        promise: inspect(promise_result), peer_result: inspect(peer_terminal),
        peer_down: inspect(peer_down), repeated_original_completion: inspect(repeated)}
      IO.puts("PUBLIC_CANCEL_REPEAT " <> JSON.encode!(row))

      assert headers == :received
      assert {:error, :cleanup_pending} = before_abort
      assert :ok = abort
      assert {:error, :aborted} = promise_result
      assert {:error, :closed} = peer_terminal
      assert peer_down in [:normal, :noproc]
      assert :ok = repeated
    end
  end

  defp capture(fun) do
    try do
      fun.()
    rescue
      error -> {:exception, error.__struct__, Exception.message(error)}
    catch
      kind, reason -> {:caught, kind, reason}
    end
  end

  defp fetch(url, opts \\ []) do
    HTTP.fetch(
      url,
      Keyword.merge(
        [
          http_version: :http1,
          http1_reuse: false,
          tls_backend: :ssl,
          redirect: :manual,
          decode_body: false,
          request_mode: :proxy,
          timeout: @timeout
        ],
        opts
      )
    )
  end

  defp peer(fun) do
    {:ok, listener} =
      :gen_tcp.listen(0, [:binary, active: false, ip: {127, 0, 0, 1}, reuseaddr: true])

    {:ok, {_, port}} = :inet.sockname(listener)
    owner = self()

    pid =
      spawn(fn ->
        try do
          {:ok, socket} = :gen_tcp.accept(listener, @timeout)

          try do
            send(owner, {:peer_result, self(), fun.(socket, owner)})
          after
            :gen_tcp.close(socket)
          end
        rescue
          error ->
            send(owner, {:peer_error, self(), Exception.format(:error, error, __STACKTRACE__)})
        after
          :gen_tcp.close(listener)
        end
      end)

    on_exit(fn ->
      stop_process(pid)
      :gen_tcp.close(listener)
    end)

    {"http://127.0.0.1:#{port}/", pid}
  end

  defp recv_head(socket, bytes \\ "") do
    if :binary.match(bytes, "\r\n\r\n") == :nomatch do
      {:ok, chunk} = :gen_tcp.recv(socket, 0, @timeout)
      recv_head(socket, bytes <> chunk)
    else
      bytes
    end
  end

  defp stop_process(pid) do
    monitor = Process.monitor(pid)
    if Process.alive?(pid), do: Process.exit(pid, :kill)

    receive do
      {:DOWN, ^monitor, :process, ^pid, _reason} -> :ok
    after
      @timeout -> raise "test process did not stop"
    end
  end
end

upstream_issue_draft.title: [internal] Pre-head HTTP1 cancellation can expose einval after confirmed cleanup
upstream_issue_draft.label: internal request
upstream_issue_draft.body:
**Requesting repo:** gsmlg-opt/gaoxy on branch `codex/m3-h1-resource-foundation`

**Severity:** blocker for the existing exact public pre-response-head cancellation compatibility gate. Other unblocked work can continue. No local workaround or assertion relaxation is proposed.

With the coordinated Hex HTTP Fetch/http_core/http_runtime 0.21.4 cohort, cancelling a real direct HTTP/1 request after the peer receives the complete request headers and before it sends any response sometimes returns `{:error, :einval}` from the original Promise although `HTTP.RequestCompletion.abort_and_await(original, 3000)` returned `:ok`. Expected Promise result is exactly `{:error, :aborted}`; the original cleanup handle, actual peer closure and repeated completion must still succeed within their existing finite deadlines.

**Minimal public reproduction:** use a passive loopback TCP listener; after accepting, receive until `\r\n\r\n`, notify the caller, send no response, and wait for closure. Call `HTTP.fetch(url, http_version: :http1, http1_reuse: false, tls_backend: :ssl, redirect: :manual, decode_body: false, request_mode: :proxy, timeout: 3000)`. Retain `HTTP.Promise.completion(promise)`. After the peer's real header notification, require `RequestCompletion.await(original, 0) == {:error, :cleanup_pending}`, then call `RequestCompletion.abort_and_await(original, 3000)`, `Promise.await(promise, 3000)`, observe peer closure and joined peer DOWN, and repeat `RequestCompletion.abort_and_await(original, 0)`. No response head, private process state inspection, suspension, or dependency patch is involved.

**Observed requesting-repo evidence:** unchanged `apps/gaoxy_proxy/test/http_fetch_completion_test.exs:8` failed at its exact Promise assertion (line21) in source-stable full58:845 executed/1 failure, exit2, seed33011, `ERL_FLAGS=+S 2:2`. Abort cleanup returned:ok before the failing Promise returnedeinval; subsequent peer/repeated assertions were not executed after that failure. Same-source same-seed whole-file rerun5/0 does not erase this failure. Original test SHA25629d88592b122693154e4e0d5197910c65a2a5b2de4bcfe201f651afc474c09e6. Evidence root `docs/acceptance/evidence/m3/managed-h2-fixed-endpoint/1791956542961215590`; full receipt `pre-floor-full58-1792000443558300185.json`, log SHA256624260543bec4ab490c3cd738805d3026b4d53e3ebcf93298f7302971fc23f91. Add the bounded-repeat actual results only after execution; none are claimed here.

**Source-supported race (exact failing operation remains untraced):** public RequestCompletion sends tracker:abort. `apps/http_core/lib/http/request_lifecycle.ex:373-375` sends owner:abort and directly cancels the tracked socket;475-477 applies linger and closes it. In `apps/http_fetch/lib/http/socket_client.ex:558-568`, successful buffered sending is followed by `activate_socket` before `owner_loop` consumes pendingabort. `activate_socket:1954-1962` calls `setopts(active: :once)` and returns its raw error; `fail:1567-1584` preserves non-timeout errors; `await_owner:1664-1666` forwards them; the Fetch task returns that result and Promise awaits it unchanged. Closing the socket in this interval can therefore leak socketeinval instead ofaborted. A racing final send error after partial/complete bytes reached the peer is another possible error path. The failure log alone does not identify the exact syscall/interleaving. Cleanup success is consistent: owner/task complete and DOWN settle the logical barrier, independently of the Promise error reason.

**Latest release check:** v0.21.8 published2026-10-14T10:42:42Z, commit0ca9cf01ad07b568c80e0e3d6ea84c2c6f0ee3ea. Its SocketClient and RequestLifecycle are byte-identical to installed0.21.4 (SHA2563bfd24c17fb9f3237c2c259fdc366c2df48304a0f58faf308ee87d0523519f88 and21cf5d861399587e596f1829acfef83b7ca2bbfa1d4787adee48752fbe900e89). The newer Dialer worker-exit repair does not alter this post-send cancellation path. Searches found no existing issue matching this trigger. Closed#98 concerns preserving parser errors for streamed readers; closed#6 concerns the old:httpc abort implementation; neither describes this direct-TCP pre-head Promise race.

**Expected fix and regression:** upstream must preserve cancellation classification when its own cleanup closes this still-pending request socket, while retaining genuine independent send/protocol/transport failures and all cleanup guarantees. Add deterministic upstream coverage of cancellation during post-send activation and, if applicable, final-send completion, then publish a coordinated compatible release. Requalify the unchanged public reproduction and exact requesting-repo gate. This concerns Promise cancellation reason with real wire synchronization and logical completion; no native timer/alias/ERTS ownership certification is requested.
